prompt: One expression is missing from this working program. Fill in the blank -- answer with just the missing code.
explanation: Months are numbered 1-12 but integer division works from 0, so subtracting 1 first, dividing by 3, then adding 1 back maps January-March to quarter 1, April-June to quarter 2, and so on. Dividing the raw month value by 3 would put March and June in the wrong quarter.
hints: Shift the 1-based month down to 0-based before dividing, then shift the answer back up.
